sections.h2: What does a seller need to know about Wood County, Ohio, geography and taxing districts?
sections.html:
Along the Maumee River in northwest Ohio, Wood County runs about 617 square miles of land and borders Lucas, Ottawa, Sandusky, Seneca, Hancock, Putnam and Henry counties. Toledo's metropolitan area includes it. Wood became a county in 1820, Perrysburg served as its first seat, and the seat moved to Bowling Green in 1870.

The incorporated cities are Bowling Green, Northwood, Perrysburg and Rossford, with a sliver of Fostoria. Fifteen school districts overlap the county: Anthony Wayne, Bowling Green City, Eastwood, Elmwood, Fostoria City, Gibsonburg, Lake, Lakota, McComb, North Baltimore, Northwood, Otsego, Patrick Henry, Perrysburg and Rossford. Values come from the Auditor and bills from the Treasurer, both on One Courthouse Square in Bowling Green, and ground was broken for the courthouse on November 28, 1893, after citizens chose to move the seat from Perrysburg.

sections.h2: How do Wood County ownership and housing numbers look in the Census data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 134,176 residents for July 2025, a 1.5 percent gain from the 2020 base, spread over 54,257 households. Owners live in 64.4 percent of homes from 2020 to 2024, which leaves a little over a third of households renting. The same survey counts 5,955 veterans, the group served by the Auditor's disabled veteran program.

  • The survey's midpoint home value is $227,600.
  • Owners pay a midpoint of $1,626 monthly with a mortgage and $640 without.
  • Rent at the midpoint is $972.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $74,216 in 2024 dollars.
  • The county has 58,780 housing units and issued 163 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 triennial update do to Wood County home values?
sections.html:
Countywide, residential values went up 19 percent on average, per the Auditor's press release. State law calls for a full reappraisal every six years and an update three years later. Wood County reappraised in 2023, so the 2026 update adjusts values neighborhood by neighborhood.

The new values belong to tax year 2026, collected in February and July 2027, and carry a January 1, 2026 lien date. Sales from the prior three years drive the statistics, and only arm's length sales count. A single parcel can land above or below the average because of location and condition.

Bills should not follow values one for one. According to the Auditor, House Bill 920 trims voted outside millage as values rise, House Bill 186 puts an inflation cap credit on school districts, and House Bill 335 does the same for inside millage, the unvoted portion held to 10 mills. A renewal levy keeps its current millage, a renewal with an increase adds to it, and an additional levy is a brand new tax.

sections.h2: What are the Wood County installment months, penalties and payment methods?
sections.html:
February and July are the months for real estate and manufactured home taxes, and the Treasurer picks the exact dates annually. Around 80 taxing districts each carry their own rate. The Treasurer's information page cites a 5 percent penalty for the first 10 days after the due date and 10 percent from then on.

Ways to pay a Wood County tax bill, as the Treasurer lists them
MethodDetail
OnlineTax Search on the Treasurer's site, by card or e-check, with a convenience fee the office does not collect
PhoneAutomated line, 419-359-0006

Mailed payments count by postmark. The Treasurer warns that a machine postmark may show the processing day instead of your drop-off day, so mail early or ask the post office for a hand stamp. Call 419-354-9130 with questions.

sections.h2: Where does a Wood County owner go to contest a value?
sections.html:
Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision through the Auditor, and the Auditor's real estate page says they must be filed between January 1 and March 31. The Auditor's 2026 update FAQ names March 31, 2027 for the new values. An informal review comes first for many owners.

  • Informal review needs evidence: an appraisal under two years old, three or more comparable sales between 2023 and 2025, or a sales listing.
  • The FAQ says a disputed amount above $50,000 requires a Board of Revision filing.
  • Comparable sales can be pulled with the Sales List, Sales Search or Comp Search tools, and the Comp Search is called the most useful.
  • R.C. 5715.19 allows one complaint per interim period unless a sale, casualty, major improvement or occupancy change followed the lien date.

Reach the real estate office on the second floor of the county office building at 419-354-9173.

sections.h2: Which Wood County programs lower the tax on a home or farm?
sections.html:
Four programs appear on the Auditor's tax reduction page.

  • Homestead exemption, for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. The page prints a modified adjusted gross income ceiling of $40,000 for late applicants on tax year 2025 and $41,000 for new applicants on tax year 2026, and the house must be the primary residence.
  • Disabled veteran homestead exemption, for qualified veterans or surviving spouses.
  • Owner occupied reduction, by application, for the home an owner lives in.
  • Agricultural use valuation, for 10 or more acres in farming, with a $25.00 fee on new applications and a penalty if the land is sold, drops under 10 acres or stops being farmed.

A free agricultural district application protects farmland from certain water and sewer assessments. Homestead questions go to 419-354-9167, and agricultural programs to 419-354-9174.

sections.h2: What does a Wood County seller pay when the deed transfers?
sections.html:
The Auditor's FAQ prints a conveyance fee of $3.00 for each $1,000 of purchase price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, along with a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel. Form DTE 100(EX) is the route for deeds that qualify for an exemption.

The grantee files a value statement, and under R.C. 319.202 the grantor owes the fee. The statement also asks about agricultural valuation that could bring a recoupment charge. A Sheriff Sales link sits on the Auditor's real estate page, and a 2026 pending special assessments file is posted there too.

Get the balance from the Treasurer before signing a purchase agreement, and ask the Auditor whether any special assessment is pending on the parcel.

sections.h2: How are manufactured homes taxed and transferred in Wood County?
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects two kinds of property tax, real estate under R.C. 323.12 and manufactured homes under R.C. 4503.06, and both come due in February and July. A manufactured home is billed at the combined rate of the district where it sits, and a 1998 law moved its valuation toward market value, in the way real estate is assessed.

  • Conveyance fee on a mobile home: $1.00 per $1,000 of price, rounded up to the nearest thousand, plus $0.50 per title. No money changing hands means no fee.
  • Mobile home moving permit: $5.00, with a $100.00 fine for moving one without a permit.
  • Wood County's sales tax rate is 6.75 percent, as the Auditor's FAQ states.

faqs.q: Which months do Wood County property taxes fall due?
faqs.a: February and July. The Treasurer sets the exact dates, and the penalty is 5 percent in the first 10 days after the due date and 10 percent beyond that.

faqs.q: By how much did Wood County residential values change in 2026?
faqs.a: The Auditor's press release gives a 19 percent average rise. Parcels differ by neighborhood, and House Bills 920, 186 and 335 keep bills from rising at the same pace.

faqs.q: What is the last day for a Wood County Board of Revision complaint?
faqs.a: March 31, which the Auditor's update FAQ lists as March 31, 2027 for tax year 2026. The window starts on January 1.

faqs.q: What does a Wood County deed cost at the Auditor?
faqs.a: The FAQ prints $3.00 per $1,000 of purchase price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, plus $0.50 per parcel for transfer.

faqs.q: Which Wood County office answers tax questions?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, 419-354-9130, handles payments and bills. The Auditor's real estate office, 419-354-9173, handles values. The toll free number is 866-860-4140.
